;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 North Indian Ocean cyclone season]], [[Cyclone Nisarga]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
**Severe Cyclonic Storm Nisarga makes landfall south of [[Mumbai]]. This is the first time a tropical cyclone has targeted the megacity since 1891. About 100,000 people have been evacuated from low-lying areas in the western Indian states of [[Maharashtra]] and [[Gujarat]], areas already hard-hit by the COVID-19 pandemic. [https://npr.org/2020/06/03/868469113/powerful-cyclone-makes-landfall-near-indian-city-of-mumbai (NPR)] [https://mausam.imd.gov.in/imd_latest/contents/cyclone.php (India Meteorological Department)]
*[[2019 Ridgecrest earthquakes]]
**A {{m|w|link=yes}} 5.5 aftershock to the 2019 Ridgecrest earthquakes of July 2019 takes place. It is the third-largest earthquake of the sequence, taking place only {{convert|11|km|mi}} from the [[Garlock Fault]]. [https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/preliminary-5-1-magnitude-earthquake-in-ridgecrest-felt-all-the-way-to-hollywood/2374265/ (NBC Los Angeles)] [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2020-06-03/earthquake-5-5-quake-strikes-near-ridgecrest-calif (''The Los Angeles Times'')]
*[[Norilsk oil spill]]
**[[Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] declares a [[state of emergency]] after 20,000 tons of oil leaked into the [[Ambarnaya River]] near the [[Siberia]]n city of [[Norilsk]] within the [[Arctic Circle]] on May 26, 2020. The spill happened when a [[fuel tank]] in a [[Nornickel]] NTEK power plant collapsed. Putin lambasted the company for not reporting the incident. The [[World Wildlife Fund]] said the accident is believed to be the second-largest in modern Russian history. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-52915807 (BBC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2020/jun/03/vladimir-putin-orders-state-of-emergency-huge-fuel-spill-siberia-power-plant-kerch (''The Guardian'')]

;International relations
*[[Hong Kong–United Kingdom relations]], [[2019–20 Hong Kong protests]]
**[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] announces that the [[United Kingdom]] will change its [[United Kingdom immigration law|immigration laws]] to offer a pathway to UK citizenship for all [[Hong Kong]] citizens who are eligible for [[British National (Overseas)|BN(O)]] status, if the [[government of China]] imposes new security laws on the territory. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-52900700 (BBC News)]

;Law and crime
*[[Killing of George Floyd]]
**[[George Floyd protests]]
***[[George Floyd protests in California]]
****[[Vallejo, California|Vallejo]] police announce that Sean Monterrosa, a 22-year-old Hispanic resident of [[San Francisco]], was shot and killed by police the day before at a [[Walgreens]]. Police allege that a hammer in his pocket was mistaken for a gun. Monterrosa was on his knees. [https://www.sfchronicle.com/crime/article/Attorney-identifies-SF-resident-fatally-shot-by-15315301.php?t=d760583d8b (''The San Francisco Chronicle'')]
****[[Los Angeles]] [[Mayor of Los Angeles|Mayor]] [[Eric Garcetti]] pledges to cut the budget of the [[Los Angeles Police Department]] by up to $150 million in the wake of allegations of police misconduct during protests. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2020-06-03/protests-demanding-racial-justice-gain-momentum-across-l-a#nt=7030col1-main (''Los Angeles Times'')]
***[[George Floyd protests in Texas]]
****[[Texas State University]] President [[Denise Trauth]] announces on social media that a 20-year-old African-American student protestor, Justin Howell, had been critically injured by a [[bean bag round]] fired by [[Austin, Texas|Austin]] police on Sunday. Police maintain that Howell was not the intended target. [https://www.statesman.com/news/20200603/man-injured-by-austin-police-in-protests-is-texas-state-student-university-says (''Austin American-Statesman'')]
***[[Death of David Dorn]]
****African-American former police captain David Dorn is shot and killed while trying to protect a pawn shop in [[St. Louis]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/06/03/us/david-dorn-st-louis-police-shot-trnd/index.html (CNN)]
***[[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Tom Cotton]] ([[Republican Party (United States)|R]]–[[Arkansas|AR]]) publishes a [[op-ed]] for the ''[[The New York Times|New York Times]]'' calling for the mobilization of [[United States Armed Forces|American troops]] in response to the protests. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/03/business/tom-cotton-op-ed.html (''The New York Times'')]
**The criminal charge for former [[Minneapolis Police Department|Minneapolis Police]] officer [[Derek Chauvin]] in the death of [[George Floyd]] is upgraded to [[second-degree murder]], while the three officers who helped restrain Floyd are charged with [[aiding and abetting]] murder. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/06/03/3-more-cops-charged-in-george-floyd-death-other-officers-murder-charge-upgraded.html (CNBC)]
*[[Papua conflict]], [[2019 Papua protests]]
**An [[administrative court]] in [[Jakarta]] rules that it was unlawful for the [[Government of Indonesia]] to shut down the internet in [[Papua (province)|Papua]] and [[West Papua (province)|West Papua]] during heightened security tensions caused by antiracism protests in the two provinces last year. [https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/06/03/internet-ban-during-antiracism-unrest-in-papua-deemed-illegal.html (''The Jakarta Post'')]
*Former [[Lesotho]] First Lady [[Maesiah Thabane]] is arrested on charges of murder. Her husband, former Lesotho Prime Minister [[Tom Thabane]], is also accused of murder but not formally charged. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-lesotho-politics/lesotho-former-first-lady-arrested-in-murder-case-idUSKBN23A16M (Reuters)]
*A [[Judiciary of France|court]] in [[France]] orders [[Rwanda]]n [[Rwandan genocide|genocide]] suspect [[Félicien Kabuga]] to be handed over to a [[United Nations]] tribunal for trial. Kabuga's lawyers said that their client would not receive a fair trial at a UN tribunal and that his health was too fragile to be transferred amidst the [[COVID-19_pandemic|pandemic]]. However, French justice said his transfer is "not incompatible" with the decision. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-warcrimes-rwanda/french-court-orders-rwanda-genocide-suspect-be-tried-at-u-n-tribunal-idUSKBN23A1VI?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Former [[President of Ecuador]] [[Abdalá Bucaram]] is arrested for illegal possession of weapons during a raid on his home against corruption. [https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2020/06/03/alerta-ecuador-detenido-expresidente-abdala-bucaram-tras-allanamiento-a-su-vivienda-2/ (CNN Español)]

;Science and technology
*[[SpaceX]] successfully launches and deploys 60 [[Starlink]] satellites into a [[low Earth orbit]] from [[Cape Canaveral Air Force Station]]. This brings the total number of Starlink satellites in orbit to 482. [https://www.space.com/spacex-starlink-internet-satellites-launch-success-june-2020.html (Space.com)]
